text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended Wednesday.
LONDON - British stocks fell for the first time in three sessions as worries over rising interest rates resurfaced after Tuesday's budget. The FTSE 100 index lost 19.2 points to 4,049.2.
FRANKFURT - German shares ended lower, with the 30-share DAX index losing 13.61 points to 2,797.03. In after-hours trading the DAX index stood at 2,793.86.
PARIS - French stocks edged lower on profit-taking and a drop on Wall Street. The French truckers' strike is worrying some investors. The blue-chip CAC-40 index dipped 4.31 points to 2,270.77.
ZURICH - Swiss shares ended near the day's lows in line with a weak Wall Street and easing futures prices. The All-share SPI index ended 16.30 points lower at 2,460.78.
TOKYO - Tokyo stocks ended weaker on profit-taking after three straight rising sessions. The Nikkei 225 lost 72.97 points or 0.34 percent to 21,345.28.

HONG KONG - Hong Kong stocks set another record, overcoming early weakness on futures-related buying and strength in some property developers. The Hang Seng index rose 45.62 points to close at 13,530.95.
SYDNEY - Australian shares fell, with the All Ordinaries index off 5.3 points to 2,376.7.

JOHANNESBURG - South African shares ended mostly higher after a session abbreviated by electronic trading system failures in the morning and afternoon, the Johannesburg Stock Exchange said. The industrial index rose 36 points to 8,051.4, the all-share index added 28.6 points to 6,749.9, and the gold index fell 9.7 points to 1,563.7.
